# AWS Budgets

Manage account-wide budgets and deliver supported ACTUAL alerts from user-supplied USD cost fixtures.

**Status: implemented subset.** Operation selection does not imply complete input or behavior parity.

| Contract | Current implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Service ID | `budgets` |
| Signing name | `budgets` |
| Wire protocol | AWS JSON 1.1 |
| API version | `2016-10-20` |
| Scope | Account-wide |
| Execution | Fixture-backed actual spend and ACTUAL notifications |
| Selected operations | 16 of 26 in the pinned model |

## Implemented behavior

See the [implemented feature catalogue](catalogue.md#aws-budgets) for this service's capabilities.

## Limitations and future work

- No forecasts or price estimation; FORECASTED notifications are retained but never fire. Explicit CostTypes, unsupported filters, other budget types and non-USD budgets are stored without evaluation.
- Budget actions, performance history, account notification history, auto-adjustment, billing views and modern filter expressions/metrics are unsupported.
- No CloudFormation handlers: AWS::Budgets::Budget and AWS::Budgets::BudgetsAction, CDK and awscc deployment are unavailable.
- Local one-second cadence differs from AWS billing refresh; planned limits use the latest timestamp not after evaluation time and carry forward; percentage alerts wait for an applicable limit.
- EMAIL is capture only; standard same-account SNS only; SNS topic policies are not enforced; SNS acceptance does not guarantee downstream delivery.
- Four delivery attempts with local 1/2/4-second backoff and a one-minute crash lease; final failures retained in storage; recent delivery/message diagnostics are in memory.
- Alert text approximates AWS plain-text notifications; no AWS HTML template, account masking, unsubscribe link or budget actions; completed jobs and markers are retained until budget deletion or reset.

These gaps describe current boundaries and possible follow-up slices. The [roadmap](../roadmap/index.md)
separates proposed work from registered functionality; there are no promised release dates.
